metadata.title: Claude, Demand Intake.
metadata.purpose: Answer what Claude actually needs before it can draft a demand letter -- the case, gathered first, not the letter itself. Lands the carry-out that demand-intake gathers the parties, the facts, and the leverage into one file before any drafting starts, and the draft step only ever writes what's already there.
metadata.source_note: Unlike sibling claude-for-legal redos with unfilled placeholder narration, this source sheet's narration already carries real facts (parties, facts, basis, leverage, BATNA, privilege filters; output to intake.md the demand-draft skill reads). Its named source_skill file does not exist on this machine, but that did not block this redo -- see QUESTION.md.

beats.narration_text: Someone asks whether Claude can just write their demand letter. It can't yet -- first it needs the case: the parties, the facts, the leverage. So the real question: can Claude prep for the demand letter?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. Demand-intake is a checklist, spelled out in one file, for everything a demand letter needs before any drafting starts. Skip straight to "write the letter," and there's no case in it yet -- no parties, no facts, no dollar figure. Claude can only guess.

shot.new_visual_element: A 'DEMAND LETTER' card with blank fields -- PARTIES, FACTS, AMOUNT -- each a dim question mark

production_viz.label: No case in it yet
production_viz.mechanic: A card labelled 'DEMAND LETTER' with three blank field rows inside: 'PARTIES: ?', 'FACTS: ?', 'AMOUNT: ?', each dim and unfilled. A caption fades in beneath: 'it can only guess.'

beats.narration_text: The skill walks through six things, in order: the parties, the facts, the legal basis, the leverage, the fallback if talks fail, and anything privileged that should stay out of it. Take one case: an unpaid invoice for forty thousand dollars, now sixty days late. Intake doesn't start with the letter -- it starts with those six answers.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- the six-item checklist appears one at a time; an invoice stamp card ($40,000, 60 days late) lands beside it

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- the six questions
production_viz.mechanic: Six labels appear in sequence down the left: PARTIES, FACTS, BASIS, LEVERAGE, BATNA, PRIVILEGE. Beside them, a stamped card fades in: 'INVOICE' / '$40,000' / '60 DAYS LATE'. THIS EXACT INVOICE CARD RETURNS, RESOLVED, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Fill in those six for the invoice -- the vendor, the due date, the late clause, the interest owed, the fallback of small claims -- and the letter has ground to stand on. Same six questions, every time. But only those six: a fact nobody mentions never makes it in, and this step never writes the letter itself. It hands a finished file to a separate step that drafts.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- the invoice card locks in as 'GROUND TO STAND ON', then splits into 'a fact nobody mentions -> never makes it in' and 'this step never drafts -> hands a file to the step that does'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- ground to stand on
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 INVOICE CARD RETURNS, identical placement, and the six checklist labels collapse into it one by one until it locks in, highlighted terracotta, reading 'GROUND TO STAND ON'. It then splits into two cards: left reads 'a fact nobody mentions' above 'never makes it in'; right reads 'this step never drafts' above 'hands a finished file onward', connected by a dashed line to a small second card labelled 'draft step'.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt -- read it with me. I have an unpaid invoice. Before you draft a demand letter, ask me for the parties, the facts, the legal basis, my leverage, my fallback if they don't pay, and anything privileged that should stay out of it. Then tell me what's still missing. Liam, in for Bear.
